story: At 9:17 on a partly cloudy Monday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is tinkering at his workbench in his garage, carefully tidying the golf cart wiring and running a quiet test of the amp and light strings with a content look on his face. Over at her house, Donna is planning ahead, reserving a two-hour court slot on the club calendar for herself and Gary and marking their first ladder match with determination. Out on Magnolia Loop, Hal is counting the pink flamingos visible from the street so he can report the total to the review committee, while at his house, Rosa is flipping through the latest pages of her violation notebook, looking worried about where Hal has been.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Tidy the cart wiring and run a low-volume test of the amp and light strings
Donna (donna club calendar): Reserve a 2-hour court slot for Gary and me and mark our first ladder match
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total for the review committee
Rosa (hal violation notebook): Flip through the latest pages for any sign of where Hal's been

gary.thought_process: It's Monday morning and I'm at home with the cart. Last tick I wired the speaker amp and light strings into the battery, all kept inside the garage out of street view, which keeps me clear of L-01 until Architectural Review signs off. I filed the modification form back around tick 35, so the approval should be moving. Holiday lighting isn't allowed until Thanksgiving anyway, so there's no rush to show anything off. Best use of this hour is to finish the build: test the wiring, check the connections, and make sure the amp is quiet enough to test without breaking any amplified-sound rules (it's well past 7 AM, so L-03 is fine). I'll go to the workbench and tidy up the wiring and run a low-volume bench test. Being useful with my hands is what I'm best at, and it keeps the loneliness at bay.

parameters.content: Tidy the cart wiring and run a low-volume test of the amp and light strings

donna.thought_process: It's Monday morning and nobody is around. Pruitt-Kowalski is on the ladder now, and I'm already packing my bag, so the next step is getting our first match on the books. I just checked the calendar last tick, and the dinner at Rosa's last night went well. Rosa mentioned she hadn't seen Hal or Gary, which is a little worrying, but I can check on Gary once we're at the court. Best use of this hour is to pin down open court time with the club calendar, keeping within the 2-hour reservation limit, so I can text Gary a real time for practice.

parameters.content: Reserve a 2-hour court slot for Gary and me and mark our first ladder match

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop at 9:17 on a Monday with no one around. Notebook's already got my dated notes on Gary's cart and Donna's flamingos from last tick. The flock is right here in the zone, so I can do an actual count and get the number right before this goes to the committee. L-02 says three ornaments max visible from the street, and a vague accusation won't hold up. Facts will. I'll count them properly, by the book. Though if she's kept her promise on the flamingos, I may have to eat my words.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and note the total for the review committee

rosa.thought_process: I'm at Hal's house at 9:17 AM and nobody is in sight. Hal didn't show up to the dinner and I've been worried something happened. I walked over to check on him, but the porch is empty. His binoculars and violation notebook are sitting right here, which is very Hal. I can't speak to anyone, and wandering off would waste the trip. Looking at what he's been keeping an eye on might tell me where he is, or whether he's just been busy with his usual neighborhood watch. As an ER nurse, I'd rather know he's okay than assume. I'll look at the notebook for clues about his recent days.

parameters.content: Flip through the latest pages for any sign of where Hal's been

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
